description:
## Goal
Make the ordinary expression parser the sole authority for `when` and for which no-parens call owns a trailing `do` block. A generic call such as `def foo(x) when guard, do: body` must quote correctly before definition semantics know or care that the callee is def.

## Paper contract
- `def foo(x) when x > 0, do: x` -> `def(when(foo(x), x > 0), [do: x])`.
- `a = b when c` -> `when(=(a, b), c)`.
- `a when b = c` -> `when(a, =(b, c))`.
- `outer inner() do body end` -> `outer(inner(), [do: body])`.
- `outer(inner() do body end)` -> `outer(inner([do: body]))`.
These are parser contracts, not definition-specific rewrites.

## Strategy
Refactor the Pratt loop so an already-parsed lhs can continue through the same infix authority. Add Tok::When to that authority as a right-associative operator at Elixir relative precedence: weaker than `=` and `::`, stronger than comma/clause separators. Suppress trailing-do capture while reading each no-parens argument, then let the outer call attach it; explicit parentheses re-enable inner ownership.

Delete the case-clause guard constructor and every other binary `when` constructor that the general expression path makes redundant. Named fn/fnp parsing is temporary scaffolding until the final cutover, but if its head must start through a dedicated routine, feed that lhs into the same Pratt suffix rather than manufacturing a second when node. Anonymous multi-argument clauses may retain only the clause-shape adapter needed for Elixir AST `when(arg1, arg2, guard)`; it must not decide precedence or parse the guard through a second grammar. Extern `when` constraints remain explicitly separate because they describe type variables, not guard expressions.

## TDD and signal
Start with frontdoor tests built from `Code.string_to_quoted` oracle outputs for the five paper examples. Add guarded case, receive, with, single-argument lambda, multi-argument lambda, multiline operator continuation, keyword guard, and invalid-context cases. Assert full quoted shape and source spans, not only that `when` is mentioned. Run existing frontdoor, quoted-function, macro, protocol, and fixture tests.

## What goes away
Bespoke named-function and case binary guard construction; implicit permission for an inner argument call to steal the outer do block; comments/docs describing when as definition-only grammar. Update `.agent/docs/parser-syntax.md` with precedence and ownership rules.

## Acceptance
One code path parses binary when expressions. Elixir-oracled AST tests distinguish both do ownership cases. No parser regression is hidden by downstream definition canonicalization, and all warnings remain errors.

comments.text: Implemented via TDD. General binary when now has one Pratt authority; named temporary grammar feeds its parsed lhs through that suffix; case no longer constructs guards. No-parens calls suppress nested do capture while every matched boundary reopens local ownership, including capture grouping. Removed the redundant/non-Elixir completed-call comma-do attachment. Added whole-tree quoted-shape assertions and adjacent lexer/frontdoor tests, plus parser authority docs. Fresh holistic reviews found and drove the matched-boundary, capture, comma-do, and test-signal corrections. Gates: cargo test --workspace --lib (2022 passed, 6 ignored; fz_runtime 257 passed), cargo test --workspace --doc, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --all -- --check, git diff --check.

title: Make when and trailing-do ownership general expression grammar
